card.name: Modifiers before nouns in historical prose
card.fires_on: Adjectives, possessives and determiners (extensive, any, important, his, my) just before a noun, mostly in narrative history or biography text about people, towns and industries.

modes.label: Adjective before business or industry noun
modes.description: An adjective like extensive or important that opens a noun phrase about projects or industries.
modes.example: The city has<< important>> fish and fish-processing industries.

modes.label: Possessive before studies or room
modes.description: His or my placed before a noun describing a person's work or setting in a biographical passage.

modes.label: Verb or auxiliary in a life story
modes.description: A verb such as began or had in a short account of a person's career or move.
modes.example: He was a resident of Curtis Bay, and<< began>> his long career with the Curt

card.plain: It fires on small describing or owning words that come right before a noun in old-style history writing.
